claims.text: Harrison sent June 1945; visited 30 camps; report delivered to Truman 24 Aug 1945; cited Jewish Agency request for 100,000 certificates; Truman forwarded it to Attlee recommending 100,000; Attlee rejected; British set up the Anglo-American Committee to ease tensions; April 1946 report recommended 100,000.
UNSCOP 37th meeting, Jerusalem, 19 July 1947: the chairman reported on the Exodus 1947; with Mr. Simic he went to Haifa.
Aug 1947: Fabregat, Hood and Garcia Granados returned from a tour of DP camps; report described as most effective; UNSCOP considerably sobered.
Lodge-Fish resolution: House 30 June 1922, Senate 13 July, Harding signed 21 Sept 1922.

American Palestine Committee: founded 1932 (Neumann); by the 1940s 15,000 members including two-thirds of the Senate; worked with AZEC on the 1945 resolution; merged 1946 into the American Christian Palestine Committee.

entries.topic: Following the money to the central banks: documented ties between central banks and the movement, 1855–1948

claims.text: EJ via JVL: total Haavara transfer LP 8,100,000; Reichsbank provided LP 2,600,000 in coordination with Haavara; about 60,000 German Jews immigrated 1933–39 with the transfer's help; emigrants paid into the PALTREU account.

JTA 10 Aug 1934: the Reichsbank would control transferred Jewish capital even in Palestine; uncertified property passes to the Reichsbank; the money settled German export bills, giving the regime sterling.

JTA 9 Apr 1936: the Reichsbank will no longer transact business under the agreement; a government order gave operation to Haavara and two banks, the Warburg bank of Hamburg and A. E. Wassermann of Berlin.

EJ via JVL: Max Warburg appointed to the Reichsbank General Council in 1924; helped emigrants move money through the Palaestina-Treuhand; intensified interest in Zionism from the late 1920s; emigrated to New York 1938.
Alphonse de Rothschild appointed a regent of the Banque de France in 1855, a position he held for the rest of his life (d. 1905).
Palestine Currency Board appointed by the Colonial Secretary 1926, based in London, Palestine pound at par with sterling, dissolved May 1948; Anglo-Palestine Bank issued new notes August 1948.
FRUS 20 Feb 1948: the UK would block Palestine's sterling balances (about £100 million) from 22 Feb, leaving £7 million for working balances to mid-May; Palestine to leave the sterling area.
Eugene Meyer, Fed chairman 1930–33, first World Bank president 1946; the article records no position on Zionism or Palestine.
Bank Notes Ordinance 1948 effective 17 Aug 1948; Anglo-Palestine Bank Issue Department; Bank of Israel Law 24 Aug 1954; bank established 1 Dec 1954; first governor David Horowitz.
